pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all three seeded rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected. It relies on per-test storage isolation. I couldn't run it.
The `item` renderer in src/index.js prefixes '★ ' only when starred. Test 'AC-2' checks the exact list with one starred item.
The starred view filters with WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id. Test 'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and expects them in id order.
`/` and `?show=all` use the unfiltered query ORDER BY id. Test 'AC-4' covers both paths.
Each view carries its link in VIEWS. Test 'AC-5' checks the exact anchors on both views.
Object.hasOwn(VIEWS, show) rejects other values with a 400 before any query runs. Test 'AC-6' covers 'Starred', 'none', empty and '__proto__', and checks there is no <li>.
traffic/routes.json is now ["/", "/?show=starred"]. Test 'AC-7' asserts it. The traffic Worker builds the URL by string concatenation, so the query is preserved.

findings.what: The route validation regex now allows a query string, but the error message still says 'array of paths starting with "/"'. It no longer says that queries are allowed.
findings.fix: Reword the message to say that paths may carry a query and must not contain spaces or '#'.

lenses.note: The spec has an owner go dated 2026-10-12. The change matches its decisions: starred items keep their place, and the view is a query parameter.
All 7 acceptance items are implemented and each is named by a test. All four state-table rows have a test. The spec was added in the same commit as the code and edited by no later commit.

The tests assert exact output and would fail if the code were wrong. I couldn't run them here because vitest isn't installed. The traffic fake-app change and the new shell cases add coverage and loosen nothing.
README describes ?show=starred. No stale docs found.
The SQL is built only from a fixed VIEWS table, and the key is validated with hasOwn. No defects found beyond the low finding.
The show parameter is checked against an allowlist. Titles stay escaped. No injection found.
The page markup changed (a nav link and ★ markers), but the repo has no styling or UI framework. Nothing to judge beyond the HTML that the tests check.
No browser or UI tooling is available. The page is plain server-rendered HTML, and the PR states there are no screenshots.
The title is not literally given, only a heading, and it describes the change. The claims about migrations, routes, the README and the traffic check match the diff.
